sentences.text: Researchers used a rat model of traumatic brain injury created by controlled cortical impact, where animals received two one-hour inhalations of 4% hydrogen gas.
In these injured rats, breathing hydrogen gas was associated with less swelling in the brain and fewer signs of neurological damage.
The treatment led to a higher count of M2-type microglia and a lower count of M1-type microglia, while also lowering the activity of the genes Jak2, Stat1, Stat3, and Hmgb1.
The authors suggest that the protective effect of hydrogen may work by blocking the JAK/STAT signaling pathway, which in turn changes how microglia cells behave.
